plan.goal: Size the PLINK binary .bed dataset and per-chromosome files for a GWAS genotype cohort of 18636 samples and 1152885 variants (168804 on the largest chromosome).
plan.rationale: The .bed binary format packs 2 bits per sample per variant (4 samples/byte). Total .bed size = n_samples × n_variants / 4 / 1e6 MB. Per-chromosome .bed size uses the same rule applied to the largest chromosome's variant count (168804). The number of per-chromosome files corresponds to the number of chromosomes in the dataset; assuming a standard human reference genome (GRCh37/GRCh38), this is 25 (22 autosomes + X + Y + MT).
caveats: Number of per-chromosome files assumes a standard human reference genome (22 autosomes + X + Y + MT = 25). Verify against the actual chromosome list in the .bim file — if Y or MT are absent (e.g. female-only cohort or array without those markers), the file count will be lower.
The per-chromosome .bed size (786.46 MB) is for the largest chromosome (168804 variants); other chromosomes with fewer variants produce proportionally smaller files.
Total .bed size (5371.29 MB) should equal the sum of all per-chromosome files; confirm the variant count is post-QC (after filtering) before relying on the disk budget.
